# Integer Multiplier FL Model

from pymtl3 import *
from pymtl3.stdlib.stream.ifcs import IStreamIfc, OStreamIfc
from pymtl3.stdlib.stream      import IStreamDeqAdapterFL, OStreamEnqAdapterFL

class IntMulFL( Component ):

  # Constructor

  def construct( s ):

    # Interface

    s.istream = IStreamIfc( Bits64 )
    s.ostream = OStreamIfc( Bits32 )

    # Queue Adapters

    s.istream_q = IStreamDeqAdapterFL( Bits64 )
    s.ostream_q = OStreamEnqAdapterFL( Bits32 )

    s.istream //= s.istream_q.istream
    s.ostream //= s.ostream_q.ostream

    # FL block

    @update_once
    def block():
      if s.istream_q.deq.rdy() and s.ostream_q.enq.rdy():
        msg = s.istream_q.deq()
        s.ostream_q.enq( msg[32:64] * msg[0:32] )

  # Line tracing

  def line_trace( s ):
    return f"{s.istream}(){s.ostream}"

#=========================================================================
# verify_build_tag.py
#=========================================================================
# Standalone verification script for the profiling instrumentation run.
#
# It imports every module modified to carry a BUILD_TAG (7 modules from
# lab2_proc and 3 modules from lab1_imul), asserts each module defines
# BUILD_TAG == 'profiling', asserts all ten values are one shared
# identical value, and prints a per-module PASS line.
#
# Run it standalone from the sim/ directory:
#
#   % cd sim
#   % python3 verify_build_tag.py
#
# Note on imports: we use importlib.import_module with fully-qualified
# absolute module names instead of "from lab1_imul import IntMulFL",
# because lab1_imul/__init__.py re-exports same-named classes, and the
# class binding would shadow the module we actually need to check.

import os
import sys

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sys.path bootstrap
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# conftest.py (used by pytest) normally puts sim/ on sys.path. For robust
# standalone runs we prepend this file's directory (sim/) ourselves so the
# absolute imports below always resolve, regardless of the cwd.

SIM_DIR = os.path.dirname( os.path.abspath( __file__ ) )
if SIM_DIR not in sys.path:
  sys.path.insert( 0, SIM_DIR )

import importlib

EXPECTED_TAG = 'profiling'

# Fully-qualified names of all 10 modules modified for profiling.
MODULE_NAMES = [
  'lab2_proc.ProcAlt',
  'lab2_proc.ProcBase',
  'lab2_proc.ProcDpathAlu',
  'lab2_proc.ProcDpathImmGen',
  'lab2_proc.ProcFL',
  'lab2_proc.tinyrv2_encoding',
  'lab2_proc.tinyrv2_semantics',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulAlt',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulBase',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulFL',
]

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# main
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():

  tag_values = {}
  problems   = []

  # Import and check each module, one at a time, reporting PASS/FAIL per
  # module so a single failure does not hide the status of the others.

  for name in MODULE_NAMES:

    try:
      module = importlib.import_module( name )
    except Exception as err:
      problems.append( f'{name}: import failed: {err!r}' )
      print( f'FAIL {name}: could not import ({err!r})' )
      continue

    assert hasattr( module, 'BUILD_TAG' ), \
        f'{name}: module has no BUILD_TAG attribute'

    value = getattr( module, 'BUILD_TAG' )

    assert value == EXPECTED_TAG, \
        f"{name}: BUILD_TAG == {value!r}, expected {EXPECTED_TAG!r}"

    tag_values[ name ] = value
    print( f"PASS {name}: BUILD_TAG == 'profiling'" )

  # Every one of the 10 modules must have been imported and passed.

  assert len( tag_values ) == len( MODULE_NAMES ), (
      f'only {len(tag_values)}/{len(MODULE_NAMES)} modules passed:\n  '
      + '\n  '.join( problems )
  )

  # All collected BUILD_TAG values must be one shared, identical value.

  unique_tags = set( tag_values.values() )

  assert len( unique_tags ) == 1, (
      f'BUILD_TAG values are not identical across modules: {tag_values!r}'
  )

  assert unique_tags == { EXPECTED_TAG }

  print( f'ALL PASS: {len(MODULE_NAMES)} modules agree on '
         f"BUILD_TAG == 'profiling'" )

if __name__ == '__main__':
  main()

#=========================================================================
# verify_build_tag.py
#=========================================================================
# Standalone verification script for the profiling instrumentation run.
#
# It imports every module modified to carry a BUILD_TAG (7 modules from
# lab2_proc and 3 modules from lab1_imul), asserts each module defines
# BUILD_TAG == 'profiling', asserts all ten values are one shared
# identical value, and prints a per-module PASS line.
#
# Run it standalone from the sim/ directory:
#
#   % cd sim
#   % python3 verify_build_tag.py
#
# Note on imports: we use importlib.import_module with fully-qualified
# absolute module names instead of "from lab1_imul import IntMulFL",
# because lab1_imul/__init__.py re-exports same-named classes, and the
# class binding would shadow the module we actually need to check.

import os
import sys

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# sys.path bootstrap
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# conftest.py (used by pytest) normally puts sim/ on sys.path. For robust
# standalone runs we prepend this file's directory (sim/) ourselves so the
# absolute imports below always resolve, regardless of the cwd.

SIM_DIR = os.path.dirname( os.path.abspath( __file__ ) )
if SIM_DIR not in sys.path:
  sys.path.insert( 0, SIM_DIR )

import importlib

EXPECTED_TAG = 'profiling'

# Fully-qualified names of all 10 modules modified for profiling.
MODULE_NAMES = [
  'lab2_proc.ProcAlt',
  'lab2_proc.ProcBase',
  'lab2_proc.ProcDpathAlu',
  'lab2_proc.ProcDpathImmGen',
  'lab2_proc.ProcFL',
  'lab2_proc.tinyrv2_encoding',
  'lab2_proc.tinyrv2_semantics',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulAlt',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulBase',
  'lab1_imul.IntMulFL',
]

#-------------------------------------------------------------------------
# main
#-------------------------------------------------------------------------

def main():

  tag_values = {}
  problems   = []

  # Import and check each module, one at a time, reporting PASS/FAIL per
  # module so a single failure does not hide the status of the others.

  for name in MODULE_NAMES:

    try:
      module = importlib.import_module( name )
    except Exception as err:
      problems.append( f'{name}: import failed: {err!r}' )
      print( f'FAIL {name}: could not import ({err!r})' )
      continue

    assert hasattr( module, 'BUILD_TAG' ), \
        f'{name}: module has no BUILD_TAG attribute'

    value = getattr( module, 'BUILD_TAG' )

    assert value == EXPECTED_TAG, \
        f"{name}: BUILD_TAG == {value!r}, expected {EXPECTED_TAG!r}"

    tag_values[ name ] = value
    print( f"PASS {name}: BUILD_TAG == 'profiling'" )

  # Every one of the 10 modules must have been imported and passed.

  assert len( tag_values ) == len( MODULE_NAMES ), (
      f'only {len(tag_values)}/{len(MODULE_NAMES)} modules passed:\n  '
      + '\n  '.join( problems )
  )

  # All collected BUILD_TAG values must be one shared, identical value.

  unique_tags = set( tag_values.values() )

  assert len( unique_tags ) == 1, (
      f'BUILD_TAG values are not identical across modules: {tag_values!r}'
  )

  assert unique_tags == { EXPECTED_TAG }

  print( f'ALL PASS: {len(MODULE_NAMES)} modules agree on '
         f"BUILD_TAG == 'profiling'" )

if __name__ == '__main__':
  main()
